headline: The OLS return to schooling has roughly doubled since 1979 (0.063 → ~0.092–0.100 in 2024), while AK91's headline IV≈OLS finding survives only as a point estimate — first-stage F≈5 makes it weak-IV-fragile, with an empty Anderson–Rubin set for the 1940s cohort.

tables.title: Lane B — IV on original data with modern inference

figures.caption: AK91 living update. Panel A: OLS return to schooling for men 40–49, 1969→2024 (package anchors + TSLS/AR at 1969/79; ACS 2005–2024). Panel B: first-stage Q1 education deficit attenuating across birth decades, with no public QOB data after the 1949 cohort. Panel C: 16–17-year-old enrollment near-universal, the law's bite falling to ~0.
figures.alt: Three stacked panels. Top: OLS return rising from ~0.07 in 1969/79 to ~0.12 around 2010 then easing to ~0.09 by 2024, with weak-IV TSLS/AR intervals at 1969 and 1979. Middle: three points at birth decades 1920s/30s/40s showing Q1 deficits of -0.167, -0.119, -0.084 with a grey 'no data ≥1950' region. Bottom: enrollment shares near 0.95-0.97 across 1960-2024 with fading DiD law-effect labels.

notes: 2005–2007 ACS WKW is continuous weeks (1–52), not the 6-category interval the spec assumed (that coding began 2008); corrected in-data (else those years kept only ~2,200 vs ~181,000 records).
2020 ACS 1-Year PUMS does not exist (Census COVID gap); modern grid is 2005–2019 + 2021–2024, 2024 included.

IV series necessarily stops at the 1940–49 cohort: no public quarter-of-birth microdata after the 1980 Census and enrollment at 16 now ≈97%, so the instrument is both unavailable and economically dead.
No SMSA control exists in ACS; bridge check on package data shifts the 1979 return by only +0.0026 (<0.005). Education mapped from ACS attainment categories to years (per-mapped-year return).
